chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That he disliked prostrating on paper that has writing on it.

key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (expressing a preferred dislike, not prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to prostrate on paper with writing?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) disliked prostrating on paper containing writing, a ruling often interpreted by Shia jurists as a precaution against disrespecting the Divine Names or Quranic verses inscribed upon it. This preference underscores the broader Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) during prayer, where the physical surface of prostration is viewed as a vessel for honoring God, thereby encouraging believers to use plain earth or mats rather than surfaces bearing sacred text.
